posts.title: A distraction-free book editor built from ttyd, micro, and a Raspberry Pi
posts.description: I write long texts in Markdown. And I constantly look for a distraction free editor and wirting expirience . For a book project, “long” stopped meaning a few screens and started meaning a file I no longer wanted to scroll through from the top every time I opened it. posts.title: A DEC VT520 as a Linux Writing Terminal (with german umlauts)
posts.description: Using a VT520 on a Utilite Pro over a Zimodem Wi-Fi modem — with working German umlauts, UTF-8 files, and nano . This guide describes a working setup and explains how to rebuild it. It covers the two problems that cost the most time: German umlauts are garbled or missing because the VT520 speaks ISO-8859-1 / DEC character sets, while modern Linux and Hugo expect UTF-8. posts.title: Dec VT 520 Terminal
posts.description: I am a big fan of Terminals since I ever discovered them. Because I am a few years too young to truly know or use them, I am so fascinated by them. Above all, I really like the idea of a silent computer with a full keyboard that connects to an actual computer. Logging into a “mainframe” evokes, for me, the kind of charm that, back in the day, only the young Karl Koch 1 truly experienced.
